title: Joint and edge profiles for the Prairie Avenue 1904 stone library (package K02)
status: Declared with its library, not yet laid by any component. T-2289 builds the first K02 masonry from these numbers on the 1808 Prairie exemplar; until then nothing in the scene reads this file.
rule: The maps carry what lies inside one stone's face. Everything at the scale of a stone (its course, its joint, its arris, its chips, its rock-faced projection) is GEOMETRY a component builds from the numbers below, in metres, in the K01 component frame. The one exception is random rubble, which has no courses to build and carries its pattern in its map (pattern_in_map).
bound: Course heights, joint width and rock-faced relief are bounded by the one Prairie Avenue wall whose courses are transcribed: Glessner's street granite, 24 courses of 7.5-20 in, a 0.025 ft joint and 0.025-0.15 ft of rock-faced relief (data/structures/glessner_house.json v4_detail, from HABS sheet 5). That is an ANALOGUE for the other houses, not a reading of them. Brickwork's 6-12 mm joint and the stair and wall ranges are RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's starting priors. Every other figure here is ours.
replaceable_by: a photograph, drawing or specification of a named house's stonework replaces its fabric's numbers for that house, in that house's own record; this file stays the default for a house nothing describes.

common.nonrepeat: Each block samples its own window of the tile: a per-block UV offset in [0, 1) on both axes and a coin-flip mirror in u, drawn from the block's seed (K01 seed rule: component id + instance + block index, never a clock or a counter). Two adjacent blocks never share a window, so no course repeats the one beside it.
common.bed_orientation: Image x lies along the stone's natural bed. A walling block lays it horizontal. A VOUSSOIR turns it so the bed runs along the voussoir's radial joint, perpendicular to the arch's thrust, as a mason sets a bedded stone in an arch; a lintel, sill, coping or belt course lays it along its length.
common.chips: Sparse: chips eat into the arris, never widen the joint or grow the stone past its course, and never sit on two consecutive blocks' same corner.
common.unassigned: Three register rows say only 'limestone' (pa-2110-30, pa-2018-s.-calumet-avenue-31, pa-1936-s.-michigan-avenue-32): Lemont or Bedford is their house tickets' to read, not this file's to guess. One row names marble trim (pa-2126-20); the library has no marble, and that house's ticket brings it.
common.mortar: The sandy lime of assets/textures/glessner-v4 mortar, shared; a recess is geometry, so the mortar face sits recess_m behind the arris line.

granite_rock_faced.course_rule: alternating high and low courses allowed, as Glessner's street walls run; one course's height holds along its whole run

corner_bond.rule: quoins return alternately on each face, long and short

granite_rock_faced.uses: rock-faced bases, area walls, steps and copings where a structure record names granite
granite_rock_faced.not_for: a default for any house. None of the study's 62 register rows names granite; Glessner, the one granite house on the avenue, keeps its own library (assets/textures/glessner-v4/). A house wears this only on its own record's word (T-1844: granites must not be painted onto every mansion).

sandstone_brown.course_rule: regular courses on a street front; a rock-faced brownstone front takes rock_face_projection_m, a smooth one none

corner_bond.rule: ashlar quoins return alternately long and short

sandstone_brown.uses: the brownstone and brown-sandstone fronts, bands, basements and copings the register names
sandstone_brown.not_for: a Bedford or Lemont front; the register's word for each house decides which stone it is

limestone_lemont.course_rule: coursed in the local quarry's beds, which run thinner than a cut freestone's

corner_bond.rule: quoins return alternately long and short

limestone_lemont.uses: the Lemont-limestone fronts the register names, and an undocumented foundation or rear wall in local stone

limestone_bedford.course_rule: large sawn freestone blocks in regular courses

corner_bond.rule: quoins return alternately long and short

limestone_bedford.uses: the Bedford-stone envelopes the register names

dressed_trim.course_rule: one piece per sill, lintel, belt, coping, voussoir or carved block; the piece's own length, never a repeated module
dressed_trim.uses: smooth trim on any masonry front: sills, lintels, belts, copings, voussoirs and the blocks carving is cut in
dressed_trim.not_for: a whole wall; a smooth ashlar front is its stone's own fabric laid smooth

foundation_rubble.course_rule: none: random rubble has no courses, so its stones and its mortar are in the map at 0.15-0.45 m across with an 18-30 mm joint recessed about 15 mm

corner_bond.rule: a dressed quoin of the house's trim stone at each exposed corner

foundation_rubble.uses: foundations above grade, basement area walls and the rear and service walls of a house whose record names no other foundation
